title: Polynomial rings in finitely many variables over a field are factorial
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $n\geq0$ an integer, and put $A=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] (so $A=k$ for $n=0$). Then $A$ is a unique factorization domain: $A$ is an integral domain (a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors), and every nonzero nonunit of $A$ is a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and multiplication by units. Here an element is prime if it is nonzero, not a unit, and divides a product only if it divides one of the factors.

UniqueFactorizationMonoid together with IsDomain is the standard UFD notion (Mathlib/RingTheory/UniqueFactorizationDomain/Defs.lean:133-137). For a nonunit the multiset is nonempty, so an overall unit can be absorbed into one prime factor. All indicated local source lines were read on 2026-10-23. No finiteness or positive-number-of-variables hypothesis is imposed by the instances, so n = 0 is included.
